analysis.answer: Current law allows individuals 21 or older who lawfully possess a handgun to carry it concealed without a permit. This measure removes that provision, instead requiring a concealed carry permit issued by the county sheriff.

Applicants will incur the direct financial costs and the time opportunity cost of completing the mandated eight-hour safety course. County sheriffs will bear the administrative costs of processing applications and verifying course completion.
Individuals who wish to carry a concealed handgun will pay the time and financial costs of the required training. Firearms safety instructors will benefit from the increased demand for their courses.

Demand for certified firearms safety instructors will likely increase. Some individuals who currently carry a concealed handgun without a permit may choose to stop carrying rather than invest the time and money required to obtain the newly required permit.

The measure addresses the perceived safety risks of untrained individuals carrying concealed firearms in public. It uses a mandate requiring an eight-hour safety course to ensure that those who carry have received a baseline of formal training.

County sheriffs gain the administrative authority to issue permits. Instructors who provide the mandated eight-hour safety course gain a captive market of applicants who must use their services to comply with the law.

The impact of concealed carry permit requirements and mandatory training on public safety and crime rates is empirically disputed. Some researchers find that stricter carry laws reduce violent crime and accidental firearm injuries, while others find they have no significant impact or may hinder lawful self-defense.
